requirements.text: Proposal due September 30, 2026; procurement page lists close date September 30, 2026.
Four-month firm-fixed-price single-award strategic/assessment engagement; no build/deploy/operate/modify capabilities.
Three-year AI Implementation Strategy covering traditional/statistical, generative, and exploratory agentic AI.
Target-state operating model, governance framework, agentic-AI evaluation, and executable pilot recommendation.
Executive briefing and final readout; formal deliverable acceptance uses USAC DAF process.
Named AI Subject Matter Expert plus at most three additional key personnel; named personnel may be prime or proposed teaming partner/subcontractor personnel.
Provide two to three recent similar corporate past-performance contracts with reachable references; prior-employer individual experience is not corporate past performance.
Teaming-partner/subcontractor corporate past performance may be evaluated if properly proposed.
Technical proposal must explain how services will be performed; merely repeating the RFP is technically unacceptable.
Describe proposed AI use in technical approach; provide separate bid-sheet scenarios with and without AI when AI is proposed.
Actual AI tool/service/code use during performance requires prior written USAC approval.
Volume limits: Corporate <=4 pages, Technical <=12 pages excluding resumes, Past Performance <=5 pages, Price <=4 pages.
Each proposal volume submitted as separate PDF in one email to Procurement@usac.org and Noor.Jalal@usac.org; bid sheet may also be Excel.
Signed confidentiality agreement accompanies proposal and is outside volume page limits.
Evaluation factors: Technical, Past Performance, Price; technical subfactors descending: Technical Approach, Capabilities, Key Personnel.
Price must be realistic and reasonable; down-select may focus primarily on price and reject materially high or unrealistically low offers.
Services performed within United States; onsite expectation applies to personnel whose session requires in-person presence, not all staff every week.
Microsoft Copilot rollout is part of current state and should be assessed across governance, adoption, workforce readiness, licensing/cost, security, use cases, and value measurement.
